sentences.text: Leave granted.
2. By the impugned order, the High Court has rejected the appellants prayer for bail in anticipation of arrest.

3. The appellant is an accused in FIR No.94 of 2024 registered with Police Station Shaheen Bagh,
Delhi for offence(s) punishable under Sections 376/498A/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant, the respondent-State as well as the victim.

5. Taking note of the facts that the principal accused (father-in- law of the victim) has been granted pre-arrest bail, the co- accused (mother-in-law and sister-in-law of the victim) have been granted bail, the appellant has not been charged with any offence under the Arms Act and that there is no medical report on record establishing physical assault on the victim by the appellant, we are inclined to accept the appeal and grant relief as claimed.

6. Accordingly, it is directed that in the event of the appellant being arrested in connection with proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR, he shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial court on terms and conditions to be imposed by the trial court.

7. Needless to observe, the appellant shall make himself available for interrogation as and when required and also that he shall not, directly or indirectly, by inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such facts to any police officer or to the court.
8. Recording the aforesaid, the impugned order is set aside, and the appeal is accordingly allowed in the aforesaid terms.
